discussion.text:
KEY MESSAGES...

- A cold front will continue sliding southeastward today with
  some showers possible as it does so.

- A lull in greater rain chances is expected later this
  afternoon into tonight, but another round of showers and 
  storms is expected Thursday and Thursday night.

- There is a Marginal Risk of severe storms (mainly wind) along
  and south of US Route 24 for Thursday evening. Confidence in 
  severe weather is low.

- Turning much cooler and windy for Friday with some lake effect
  rain showers.

&&

posts.title: One more summer-like day near 83, then showers and storms late tonight
posts.summary: A sunny, unusually warm Tuesday near 83 gives way to showers and storms likely after midnight into early Wednesday, a soaking Thursday, a cool, dry weekend, and no watches, warnings or advisories for La Porte County.
body: Automatic update, 11:17 p.m.: The Special Weather Statement for northern La Porte County has ended. Since the Scoop below was written, NWS has lowered its chance of rain for Wednesday to 20% (from 40%). Over the next 12 hours, NWS's hour-by-hour forecast has rain possible from midnight to 1 a.m. (up to 43%), rain likely from 1 a.m. to 4 a.m. (up to 72%) and rain possible from 4 a.m. to 5 a.m. (up to 45%). There are no watches, warnings, or advisories for La Porte County right now.

A great day to be outside before tonight's rain. NWS says sunny, high near 83, dry through work hours. Tonight a chance of showers and storms 10 p.m. to 1 a.m., then likely (70%), low around 62. The La Porte airport at 5:15 a.m.: clear and 70. Bring in anything you want kept dry.

Wednesday: showers possible before 10 a.m. (40%), mostly dry after about 7 a.m., near 71; NWS's amounts for tonight and Wednesday add up to 1 to 1½ inches. Thursday: rain likely, then storms into the night (90%), another half to three-quarters of an inch, near 65. Friday breezy, near 57, 30% showers. Dry, chilly weekend: highs 57 to 64, a low near 35 Saturday night. NWS says a low of 62 Wednesday morning and a high of 65 Thursday; the computer models we also check say 57 and 69, so our forecast uses those. The models disagree on Wednesday and Thursday, so those days are less certain.

What changed since yesterday's Scoop: tonight's rain arrives a bit later, around 10 p.m. to 1 a.m. (from after 7 p.m.), and Wednesday's daytime chance is down to 40% (from 70%). NWS Northern Indiana forecasters say highs may near records today, thunder chances tonight look low, and the weekend chill should be brief. For Monday, our Oct. 10 Scoop said a high of 83 and a low of 57; the La Porte airport got 88 and 52.

Right now there are no watches, warnings or advisories for La Porte County or for Porter and Lake counties next door. SPC shows no severe-storm risk here through Thursday, only general thunderstorms. WPC puts La Porte in a marginal (at least 5%) risk of flooding rain from 7 a.m. Thursday to 7 a.m. Friday.

posts.title: Foggy start, then near 84 for Columbus Day; showers and storms Tuesday night
posts.summary: Morning fog gives way to a sunny, unusually warm Columbus Day near 84 and a similar Tuesday, with showers and storms likely Tuesday night into Wednesday, rain Thursday, a chilly weekend, and no watches, warnings or advisories for La Porte County.
body: Automatic update, 3:17 p.m.: Since the Scoop below was written, NWS has raised its high for today to 87 (from 84). It's running warmer than NWS's earlier hour-by-hour forecast: at 2:35 p.m. the La Porte airport reported clear and 88 degrees, where that forecast had about 83. There are no watches, warnings, or advisories for La Porte County right now.

Foggy start, then summer-like warmth for Columbus Day. Patchy fog until about 8 a.m., then mostly sunny and dry all day, high near 84, gusts to 25 mph. Tonight: mostly clear and mild, low around 69. The La Porte airport at 5:15 a.m.: fog, 54, visibility a quarter mile. Allow extra time and use low beams on the morning drive.

Tuesday: sunny, near 84. Showers and storms are likely (70%) after 7 p.m. Tuesday and through Wednesday, about half an inch to an inch added up from NWS's amounts; Wednesday near 71. Rain showers Thursday (80%), near 68, then a 30% chance Friday, near 57. A chilly, dry weekend: Saturday near 55, a low around 35 Saturday night, Sunday sunny near 61. NWS says lows of 69 tonight and 62 Wednesday morning; the computer models we also check run cooler, so our forecast says 66 and 57. The models disagree on Tuesday through Thursday, so those days are less certain.

What changed since Saturday's Scoop: Tuesday is much warmer and dry by day, near 84 (from 73); the rain now arrives Tuesday night instead (from Monday night into Tuesday morning), and Wednesday's chance is up to 70% (from 30% to 50%). NWS Northern Indiana forecasters say highs could near records today and Tuesday, and it's unclear how fast the front sinks south midweek. Yesterday we said a high of 73; the La Porte airport got 75.

Right now there are no watches, warnings or advisories for La Porte County, northern or southern, or for Porter and Lake counties next door. SPC shows no severe-storm risk here through Wednesday, only general thunderstorms possible Tuesday. WPC puts La Porte in a marginal (at least 5%) risk of flooding rain from 7 a.m. Thursday to 7 a.m. Friday.

posts.title: Automatic NWS update: Patchy fog, low around 55
posts.summary: The Daily Scoop is running late, so here is the official NWS forecast for La Porte, posted automatically at 6:32 a.m. and refreshed at 11:47 p.m.
body: This is an automatic update, refreshed through the day (latest at 11:47 p.m.). The Daily Scoop didn't post by 6:30 a.m., so here is the official National Weather Service forecast for La Porte, in NWS's own words. If Scoop's write-up comes in later today, it will replace this.

Overnight: Patchy fog. Mostly clear, with a low around 55. South wind around 5 mph. Columbus Day: Patchy fog before 6 a.m. Mostly sunny, with a high near 84. Southwest wind 5 to 10 mph, with gusts as high as 25 mph. At 11:15 p.m. the La Porte airport reported fog and 54 degrees. NWS last updated this forecast at 10:45 p.m.

The next few days, from the same NWS forecast: Monday Night: Mostly clear, low around 69. Tuesday: Sunny, high near 83. Tuesday Night: Showers and thunderstorms likely, low around 61, 60% chance of rain. Wednesday: Rain showers likely, high near 70, 60% chance of rain. Wednesday Night: Slight chance rain showers, low around 53, 20% chance of rain. Thursday: Rain showers likely, high near 67, 60% chance of rain.
Right now (checked at 11:47 p.m.): NWS has a Special Weather Statement for La Porte County until 1 a.m. Monday. We pass these along as NWS issues them; details and updates are at weather.gov/iwx.
